data.body:
Fixes bug B4ff804becc: bug fixed refuses (needs-fix-task) a bug whose fix task is named only by the configured [ids].fix_task pattern: _fixing_item looks only at rec.fix_task, so completing bugfix-<bug> with --regression-test closes nothing (tests/test_id_generator_lifecycle.py::test_complete_closes_the_bug_a_configured_fix_task_names)

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B4ff804becc --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B4ff804becc --regression-test <test>` first).

data.claim: _fixing_item ignores a task named only by the [ids].fix_task pattern
data.mechanism: reads rec.fix_task only; bug found --no-task leaves it empty
data.question: why bugs_closed empty

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s stated intent is to first add a regression test proving that `complete bugfix-<bug> --regression-test ...` closes a bug whose fix task exists only through the configured `[ids].fix_task` pattern. The manifest says the change contains five files and no new files, and none of the five is `tests/test_id_generator_lifecycle.py`. Therefore the core behavior being fixed — `_fixing_item` finding the configured fix task when `rec.fix_task` is empty — has no regression test in this change. A later edit can restore the old `rec.fix_task`-only lookup and all current tests can still pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_id_generator_lifecycle.py::test_complete_closes_the_bug_a_configured_fix_task_names (missing)

chunk_findings.detail: `fix_task_for` returns the item named by `rec.fix_task` without checking whether that item is still present/queued; it only checks `rec.fix_task` truthiness and `state.items.get(...)`. The fallback path explicitly filters `not i.removed`, so removed items are evidently retained in `state.items`. Given a bug whose `fix_task` points to a removed item, `fix_task_for` returns the removed item instead of falling back to another fixing item or to `_fixing_item`’s found-item logic. `_fixing_item` then treats that removed item as the fix source, which can make `bug fixed` use a nonexistent/removed source or incorrectly refuse when the actual fix is available elsewhere.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:fix_task_for

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback chooses the first non-removed item whose `fixes_of` includes the bug, with no preference for the item being completed and no status/queued check beyond `removed`. If two items fix the same bug — for example, an older task `A` and the task `bugfix-B` being completed — and `A` appears earlier in `state.items`, `fix_task_for` returns `A`. `_fixing_item` then uses `A` as the fix source even when `ddflow complete bugfix-B --regression-test ...` is closing the bug through `bugfix-B`, so the regression check can be performed against the wrong worktree/commit or fail because `A` is not in a worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:fix_task_for

chunk_findings.detail: The test that is named for the CLI explaining why the regression check could not run no longer creates a bug with `--no-task`; it now runs `bug found ... --item T2 --summary s` without the flag. That removes the only visible CLI coverage for the explicit “bug with no fix task” scenario that `_fixing_item`’s docstring still describes. The same weakening appears in `tests/test_knowledge_lists.py:126`. As a result, a regression in which the new `fix_task_for` scan incorrectly finds a fix item for a `--no-task` bug would not be caught by these tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback `next((i for i in state.items.values() if not i.removed and bug_id in fixes_of(state, i.id, cfg)), None)` returns the first non-removed item whose `fixes_of` includes the bug, with no preference for the item being completed or for the most recent fix attempt. Given a bug `B1` whose `rec.fix_task` is empty, and `state.items` ordered so that an older item `T-old` appears before the configured fix task `bugfix-B1`, with both `fixes_of(state, "T-old", cfg)` and `fixes_of(state, "bugfix-B1", cfg)` returning `{"B1"}`, running `ddflow complete bugfix-B1 --regression-test <test>` makes `fix_task_for` return `T-old`. `_fixing_item` then returns `T-old`, so the regression check is performed against the older item’s source rather than the `bugfix-B1` source that is being completed. The new `removed` filter does not answer the previous finding that the fallback can select the wrong fixing item when more than one item fixes the same bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:fix_task_for

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback is still `next((i for i in state.items.values() if not i.removed and bug_id in fixes_of(state, i.id, cfg)), None)`, so when a bug has no usable `rec.fix_task` link it returns the first non-removed item that `fixes_of` associates with the bug, with no preference for the fix task being completed, the configured `[ids].fix_task` task, or the most recent fix attempt. The project context itself acknowledges that two items can fix one bug; in that state the choice is wrong whenever the earlier item is not the task being completed. For example, with `state.items` insertion order `[T-old, bugfix-B1]`, `T-old` not removed and `fixes_of(state, "T-old", cfg)` containing `B1`, `bugfix-B1` not removed and also containing `B1`, and `state.bugs["B1"].fix_task == ""`, `fix_task_for(state, "B1", cfg)` returns `T-old`. Then `ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:_fixing_item` returns `T-old` for `ddflow complete bugfix-B1 --regression-test ...`, so the pre-fix regression verification uses the wrong item/source: it can fail or be skipped even though `bugfix-B1` is the completed fix task, or verify against the wrong commit and close the bug without proving the completed fix. This is the previously reported fallback-order issue; the new code and the removed-linked-fix-task test do not answer it, because the fallback still selects an arbitrary first non-removed match.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:fix_task_for

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback still chooses the first non-removed item whose `fixes_of` includes the bug, and the new unit test only puts an unrelated, non-fixing `T-other` before `bugfix-B1`; it does not put another item that also fixes the bug before the configured fix task. Given a bug `B1` with empty `rec.fix_task`, `cfg.ids.fix_task="bugfix-{parent}"`, and `state.items` ordered so that an older item `T-old` appears before `bugfix-B1`, with both `fixes_of(state, "T-old", cfg)` and `fixes_of(state, "bugfix-B1", cfg)` containing `B1`, `fix_task_for` returns `T-old` solely because of dict/event-log insertion order. That is wrong because the command is supposed to identify the bug's fix task—especially the task named by the configured `[ids].fix_task` pattern, or the item being completed—not an arbitrary earlier item that merely also references the bug. The added test does not answer this case, so `ddflow bug fixed B1` / `ddflow complete bugfix-B1` can still select or complete the wrong task.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:fix_task_for
